This vignette gives a short introduction to creating customizable CPB style figures with ggcpb.

1 What is ggcpb?

ggcpb is the new version of James. It draws figures in the CPB house style from Excel or from R.

1.1 Why ggcpb instead of James?

ggcpb is more future proof. It is built on ggplot2, the most widely used plotting package in R. This brings the following benefits:

  • More possibilities. Anything ggplot2 can do, ggcpb can do. If you need an extra layer or a special annotation, you can add it. It allows for new figure types that were not possible with James, such as a donut chart.
  • Easier to maintain. ggcpb adds a thin layer to a well tested package.

1.2 What you need to know to use ggcpb in Excel

This is the general workflow to create figures with ggcpb without using R:

  1. Find the most recent ggcpb version.
  2. Copy it to the place where you want to create figures.
  3. Put your datasets in the folder data. Open params.csv in Excel and describe your figures.
  4. Start generate_plot.bat by double clicking it. This runs the generate_plot.R script. Your figures appear in the folder generated. Each image is named after its dataset. Running the script again produces updated figures. Images with the same name are replaced. A dataset or figure that fails is skipped and listed at the end, and in params_log.txt. The other figures are still saved.

Please note. The generate_plot.bat, generate_plot.R and params.csv must all be in the same folder. Within this folder, there must be a subfolder data, in which each dataset must be saved as a CSV file, and not as spreadsheet (xlsx). In Excel, choose File -> Save as -> CSV UTF-8 (comma delimited).

You do not need to know R to follow this workflow. One parameter file and one or more datasets drive everything.

  • params.csv describes your figures. Column 1 holds the parameter names, such as title, x and data. Every other column describes one figure. The row data names the dataset of the figure. All parameters and their descriptions are given in the import vignette.
  • The folder data holds your datasets. Each dataset is its own CSV file with any name, such as koopkracht.csv. The first row holds the column names. The following rows are the observations per column.

Add the row page to save a figure at full width (15.5 cm). The default is half (7.5 cm). Write the dataset name without .csv, such as koopkracht. Leave data blank to use data/data.csv. Write a;b to draw the same figure for both datasets. A figure is saved under the name of its dataset, so koopkracht gives koopkracht.png. If two figures use the same dataset, the figure number is added, such as koopkracht_1.png.

Run the script again after every change. This will update the figures. The import vignette gives a more detailed explanation and lists all settings per figure type. See vignette("import").

1.3 Use ggcpb in R

Next to plotting Excel data with ggcpb, you can also plot data that you already have in R. The caption below each figure in this introduction shows the function to use. Load the packages first.

library(conflicted) # optional, but recommended
library(ggcpb)

Each figure type has its own function.

# Line chart
cpb_line(data = df, x = year, y = value)
# Bar chart
cpb_col(data = df, x = year, y = value, fill = group)
# Area chart
cpb_area(data = df, x = year, y = value, fill = group)
# Box plot
cpb_box(data = df, x = group, p5 = p5, p25 = p25, p50 = p50, p75 = p75, p95 = p95)
# Dot plot
cpb_dot(data = df, x = term, y = estimate, lower = lower, upper = upper)
# Donut chart
cpb_donut(data = df, fill = group, y = share)
# Scatter plot
cpb_scatter(data = df, x = income, y = spending)
# Histogram
cpb_hist(data = df, x = duration)
# Map
cpb_map(data = df, region = code, value = share)

To export a figure, use save_cpb(). It writes the figure at the CPB page widths. Use page = "half" for 7.5 cm and page = "full" for 15.5 cm.

save_cpb("zonnepanelen.png", p, page = "half")

The rest of this introduction assumes that you work in Excel.

2 Figure types

Each figure below is combined with a feature that you can also use with several other plot types, if not all. The parameters and their corresponding values are portrayed next to the figure. Other settings keep their default.

The style of the figures can be set for a whole publication. See section 4.

2.1 Line with forecast

A line chart with a forecast window and an uncertainty band.

Relevant parameters

plot_type line
title Economische groei met onzekerheid
x jaar
y groei
ymin lo
ymax hi
forecast_x 2023.5
ylab %

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with line-forecast.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_line() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.1 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_line().

2.2 Columns with two axes

Two series on one figure, with the second series on the right axis. The legend tells you which axis belongs to which series.

Relevant parameters

plot_type col
title Erfenissen en erfbelasting
x jaar
y mld
fill soort
sec_y heffing
sec_limits 0;3
sec_legend_label erfbelasting
sec_ylab mld euro
ylab mld euro

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with col-secaxis.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_col() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.2 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_col().

2.3 Horizontal bars with chosen colours

The colours decide the legend. Pick them with colour_index.

Relevant parameters

plot_type col
title Zonnepanelen naar inkomen
x groep
y aandeel
fill jaar
position dodge
orientation horizontal
colour_index 2;1
value_limits 0;70
ylab inkomensgroep
xlab aandeel binnen inkomensgroep (%)

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with col-horizontal.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_col() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.3 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_col().

2.4 Line with markers in English

A line with markers suits a few ordered categories. This figure uses the English style.

Relevant parameters

plot_type line
title Preferred tax rate by age
x leeftijd
y tarief
colour erfenis
points TRUE
value_limits 0;30
style english
ylab % average rate

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with line-points.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_line() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.4 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_line().

2.5 Boxplot

A box shows the 25th to 75th percentile. The line in the box is the median. The whiskers run from the 5th to the 95th percentile.

Relevant parameters

plot_type box
title Koopkracht per inkomensgroep
x groep
p5 p5
p25 p25
p50 p50
p75 p75
p95 p95
orientation horizontal
subtitle inkomensgroep
ylab % koopkrachtmutatie

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with box.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_box() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.5 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_box().

More box plot styles are in vignette("boxplots").

2.6 Extended boxplot on a full page

The extended boxplot has the CPB ramingen-style. Through the facet parameter the data gets grouped into the year column, which results in one panel per year in the dataset. The default figure is saved at the full page width (15.5 cm) with page = full.

Relevant parameters

plot_type boxplot_extended
title Koopkracht per inkomensgroep
x groep
p5 p5
p25 p25
p50 p50
p75 p75
p95 p95
facet jaar
facet_ncol 2
ylab % koopkrachtmutatie
page full

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with box-extended.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_boxplot_extended() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.6 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_boxplot_extended().

2.7 Donut chart

Individual categories add up to 100% in the donut chart. Categories don’t need to be expressed as percentages. Any numerical values will work, as the donut chart automatically calculates the proportions.

Relevant parameters

plot_type donut
title Energiemix van huishoudens
fill bron
y aandeel
colour_index 6;5;2;4

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with donut.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_donut() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.7 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_donut().

2.8 Donut chart with leader labels

A donut can also print its labels outside the ring, on leader lines. This one uses more categories, two decimals in the percentages and colours from the extended palette.

Relevant parameters

plot_type donut
title Energiemix, met lijnlabels
fill bron
y share
label_style leader
leader_length 0.08
label_accuracy 0.01
palette extended
colour_index 8;9;5;6;12;14;15

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with donut-leader.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_donut() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.8 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_donut().

2.9 Dot plot

A dot plot shows an estimate with its interval.

With legend = filled-empty the figure has no legend, but it keeps the space of one. This gives the same panel height as a figure with a legend.

Relevant parameters

plot_type dot
title Samenhang met voorkeurstarieven
x term
y coef
lower lo
upper hi
group blok
legend filled-empty
xlab %punt verandering

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with dot.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_dot() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.9 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_dot().

2.10 Scatter plot

The parameter cut puts the purchasing power change into classes. The classes give the points their colour.

Relevant parameters

plot_type scatter
title Energierekening naar inkomen
x inkomen
y energierekening
colour koopkracht
cut -Inf;-2;-1;0;1;2;Inf
cut_labels pct
palette blues
legend_ncol 2
ylab energierekening (euro per maand)
xlab besteedbaar inkomen (euro per maand)
x_labels euro
legend_title koopkracht (%)

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with scatter.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_scatter() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.10 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_scatter().

2.11 Histogram

Relevant parameters

plot_type hist
title Verdeling van de duur
x maanden
binwidth 2
ylab aantal
xlab duur (maanden)

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with hist.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_hist() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.11 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_hist().

2.12 Classed map

The maps can display municipalities or provinces on bundled generalised CBS/Kadaster boundaries. The following map colours each Dutch municipality by class. The parameter cut makes the classes, and cut_labels = pct writes them as percentages. In R, cpb_cut() and label_pct_nl() do the same. The boundaries come with the package.

gemeenten <- tibble(code = unique(cpb_nl_geo("gemeente")$code)) |>
  mutate(aandeel = runif(n(), 5, 75),
         klasse  = cpb_cut(aandeel, breaks = c(0, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, Inf),
                           labeller = label_pct_nl()))

Relevant parameters

plot_type map
title Aandeel huishoudens met zonnepanelen
region code
value aandeel
cut 0;20;30;40;50;60;Inf
cut_labels pct
palette blues
legend_title aandeel

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with map.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_map() instead. Follow the example code in section 5.12 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_map().

More options are in vignette("maps").

3 Ggplot2 base allows for endless possibilities

Every ggcpb figure is a real ggplot2 object. This means you can stack extra functionalities to the plot in R with +.

The next figure has a sharp rise between 2020 and 2021. We add a reference line, and a text along the diagonal in dark pink italic letters. The position comes from the coordinates of the data. The angle follows the slope of the line.

stijging <- tibble(jaar = 2017:2024,
                   waarde = c(2.1, 2.3, 2.0, 1.9, 6.4, 6.8, 6.5, 6.6))

cpb_line(stijging, x = jaar, y = waarde,
         title = "Een scherpe stijging", ylab = "%") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 6, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3) +
  annotate("text", x = 2020.2, y = 4.2, label = "scherpe stijging",
           angle = 72, colour = "#a0004e", fontface = "italic",
           size = 2.4, family = cpb_font_family())

You can stack as many pieces as you need. More patterns are in vignette("annotation").

4 Settings for the whole publication

Some settings are the same for every figure of a publication. The main one is the style. Dutch is the default. An English report uses english. It sets the number format and the words, such as the forecast label.

In R, set it once at the start of the script. Every figure then uses it, unless a figure sets its own style.

options(ggcpb.style = "dutch") # or "english"

In Excel there is no single setting for all figures. Add the row style to params.csv and give every figure the same value in its column, such as english. A blank cell uses the Dutch default.

5 Example code to create figures in R

The code below creates the figures above in R. It first builds the data, then draws the figure. It is the same code that made the figures in this document. Start the script with these lines.

library(conflicted)
library(ggcpb)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

options(ggcpb.style = "dutch") # style of the whole publication

5.1 Line with forecast

groei <- tibble(jaar = 2015:2027,
                groei = round(rnorm(13, 1.5, 0.8), 1)) |>
  mutate(marge = c(rep(0, 9), 0.4, 0.9, 1.4, 1.8),
         lo = groei - marge, hi = groei + marge)
cpb_line(groei, x = jaar, y = groei, ymin = lo, ymax = hi,
         forecast_x = 2023.5,
         title = "Economische groei met onzekerheid", ylab = "%") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2015, 2027, 3), minor_breaks = 2015:2027,
                     guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE))

5.2 Columns with two axes

erfenissen <- expand_grid(
  soort = factor(c("geen aangifte", "wel aangifte"),
                 levels = c("geen aangifte", "wel aangifte")),
  jaar  = 2015:2022
) |>
  mutate(mld = c(15.0, 15.3, 15.5, 16.3, 19.4, 20.5, 22.2, 23.0,
                 5.8, 5.6, 5.6, 6.6, 6.4, 6.5, 6.8, 7.0)) |>
  left_join(tibble(jaar = 2015:2022,
                   heffing = c(1.7, 1.8, 1.8, 1.8, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6)),
            by = "jaar")
cpb_col(erfenissen, x = jaar, y = mld, fill = soort,
        sec_y = heffing, sec_limits = c(0, 3),
        sec_legend_label = "erfbelasting", sec_ylab = "mld euro",
        title = "Erfenissen en erfbelasting", ylab = "mld euro")

5.3 Horizontal bars with chosen colours

groepen <- c("tot 120% wml", "120% wml tot modaal", "1 tot 1,5x modaal",
             "1,5 tot 2x modaal", "2 tot 3x modaal", "boven 3x modaal")
zonnepanelen <- expand_grid(
  jaar  = factor(c(2021, 2024), levels = c(2024, 2021)),
  groep = factor(groepen, levels = rev(groepen))
) |>
  mutate(aandeel = c(10, 14, 19, 22, 26, 33,
                     19, 25, 31, 38, 47, 59))
cpb_col(zonnepanelen, x = groep, y = aandeel, fill = jaar,
        position = "dodge", orientation = "horizontal",
        colour_index = c(2, 1), value_limits = c(0, 70), width = 0.85,
        title = "Zonnepanelen naar inkomen",
        ylab  = "inkomensgroep", xlab = "aandeel binnen inkomensgroep (%)")

5.4 Line with markers in English

leeftijden <- c("20 to 30", "30 to 40", "40 to 50", "50 to 60", "60 to 70")
tarieven <- expand_grid(
  erfenis  = factor(c("10,000 euro", "100,000 euro"),
                    levels = c("10,000 euro", "100,000 euro")),
  leeftijd = factor(leeftijden, levels = leeftijden)
) |>
  mutate(tarief = c(14.5, 12.5, 13.5, 10.5, 8.5,
                    21.5, 18.5, 18.5, 17.5, 17.5))
cpb_line(tarieven, x = leeftijd, y = tarief, colour = erfenis,
         points = TRUE, value_limits = c(0, 30), style = "english",
         title = "Preferred tax rate by age", ylab = "% average rate")

5.5 Boxplot

raw <- tibble(
  groep      = factor(rep(groepen, each = 400), levels = rev(groepen)),
  koopkracht = rnorm(2400, mean = rep(c(-3, -1.5, 0, 1, 2, 3.5), each = 400),
                     sd = 2)
)
kk <- raw |>
  summarise(p5 = quantile(koopkracht, 0.05), p25 = quantile(koopkracht, 0.25),
            p50 = quantile(koopkracht, 0.50), p75 = quantile(koopkracht, 0.75),
            p95 = quantile(koopkracht, 0.95), .by = groep)
cpb_box(kk, x = groep,
        p5 = p5, p25 = p25, p50 = p50, p75 = p75, p95 = p95,
        orientation = "horizontal",
        title = "Koopkracht per inkomensgroep",
        subtitle = "inkomensgroep", ylab = "% koopkrachtmutatie")

5.6 Extended boxplot on a full page

kk_jaar <- bind_rows(
  mutate(kk, jaar = "2024"),
  mutate(kk, jaar = "2025", across(p5:p95, \(v) v + 0.5))
)
cpb_boxplot_extended(kk_jaar, x = groep,
                     p5 = p5, p25 = p25, p50 = p50, p75 = p75, p95 = p95,
                     facet = jaar, facet_ncol = 2,
                     title = "Koopkracht per inkomensgroep",
                     ylab = "% koopkrachtmutatie")

5.7 Donut

bronnen <- c("gas", "elektriciteit", "warmte", "overig")
energie <- tibble(bron = factor(bronnen, levels = bronnen),
                  aandeel = c(45, 30, 15, 10))
cpb_donut(energie, fill = bron, y = aandeel,
          colour_index = c(6, 5, 2, 4),
          title = "Energiemix van huishoudens")

5.8 Donut chart with leader labels

niveaus <- c("aardgas", "overig", "windenergie op land", "zonne-energie",
             "kernenergie", "windenergie op zee")
energie2 <- tibble(
  bron  = factor(c("aardgas", "windenergie op land", "overig",
                   "kernenergie", "windenergie op zee", "zonne-energie"),
                 levels = niveaus),
  share = c(40, 35, 13, 3, 2, 7)
)
# leader_length is shortened from its 0.15 default: on this narrower
# canvas the default lines push their labels past the figure's edge
cpb_donut(energie2, fill = bron, y = share,
          label_style    = "leader",
          leader_length  = 0.08,
          label_accuracy = 0.01,
          palette        = "extended",
          colour_index   = c(8, 9, 5, 6, 12, 14, 15),
          title = "Energiemix, met lijnlabels")

5.9 Dot plot

termen <- c("Werken ontmoedigd", "Ongelijkheid", "Hard werken loont",
            "Leeftijd", "Geslacht", "Kinderen")
schatting <- tibble(
  term = factor(termen, levels = termen),
  blok = factor(rep(c("Percepties", "Achtergrond"), each = 3),
                levels = c("Percepties", "Achtergrond")),
  coef = c(3.2, 2.9, -2.0, 3.5, 0.4, -1.4),
  lo   = c(-0.3, 2.1, -3.0, 2.6, -1.3, -3.3),
  hi   = c(6.6, 3.6, -1.1, 4.3, 2.2, 0.6)
)
cpb_dot(schatting, x = term, y = coef, lower = lo, upper = hi,
        group = blok, legend = "filled-empty",
        title = "Samenhang met voorkeurstarieven",
        xlab  = "%punt verandering")

5.10 Scatter plot

hh <- tibble(inkomen = round(rlnorm(400, log(2500), 0.35))) |>
  mutate(energierekening = round(90 + 0.04 * inkomen + rnorm(n(), 0, 35)),
         koopkracht      = round(rnorm(n(), (inkomen - 2500) / 1500, 2), 1))
cpb_scatter(hh, x = inkomen, y = energierekening,
            colour = cpb_cut(koopkracht, c(-Inf, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, Inf),
                             labeller = label_pct_nl()),
            palette = "blues",
            legend_ncol = 2,
            title = "Energierekening naar inkomen",
            ylab  = "energierekening (euro per maand)",
            xlab  = "besteedbaar inkomen (euro per maand)",
            x_labels = label_euro_nl(),
            legend_title = "koopkracht (%)")

5.11 Histogram

duur <- tibble(maanden = round(rgamma(1200, 8, 0.6)))
cpb_hist(duur, x = maanden, binwidth = 2,
         title = "Verdeling van de duur", ylab = "aantal",
         xlab  = "duur (maanden)")

5.12 Classed map

gemeenten <- tibble(code = unique(cpb_nl_geo("gemeente")$code)) |>
  mutate(aandeel = runif(n(), 5, 75),
         klasse  = cpb_cut(aandeel, breaks = c(0, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, Inf),
                           labeller = label_pct_nl()))
cpb_map(gemeenten, region = code, value = klasse,
        palette = "blues",
        title = "Aandeel huishoudens met zonnepanelen",
        legend_title = "aandeel")
